judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the footer newsletter field 'seu e-mail...' (type=email, name=email). It has no autocomplete attribute in the snapshot or in today's live HTML. The best argument for a pass is that type=email identifies the purpose. It does not hold up: type=email sets the data format, which would be the same for a friend's address, not the user-information purpose that H98's autocomplete="email" declares. The snapshot cannot show the remark about Chromium's form check, but it matches how Chrome's Issues panel treats fields autofill recognises, and the core sentence holds.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the footer Instagram link. Its only content is a grey PNG glyph with alt 'Instagram'. I measured the screenshot myself: the glyph is solid #aaaaaa on #fcfcfc (--white_gray_light in the live CSS), 2.26:1, below 3:1. Nothing else visually identifies this link: the 'Redes Sociais' heading does not say which network it is. I checked whether the logo exemption applies. Understanding 1.4.11 says logos shown with low contrast by author choice, not by brand rule, are not exempt (Figures 22 and 27 show this pattern), and Instagram's glyph is specified in black, white or its gradient, not grey. The live HTML and CSS match the capture; the icon images have no hover rule.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: This is the top PIX banner: a link with href javascript:void(0) that carries only tracking attributes and has no destination. It holds one visible image (the mobile copy is hidden) reading 'PAGUE COM PIX E GANHE 3% DE DESCONTO', with alt 'Banner Topo PIX 3,0%'. The sentence is true of the capture, and the live HTML is the same. The alt is an internal label ('Banner Topo') that keeps 'PIX 3,0%' but drops that it is a discount, so I lean to a 1.1.1 failure. Against that, the claim blames a missing destination when the link has none to describe, and some auditors would accept 'PIX 3,0%' as the gist, since the cards say 'Pix ... (3% desconto)'. Competent auditors could disagree both on whether the element fails and on whether the claim names the defect.

Half-opacity #757575 on white is about #bababa, 1.94:1. At 19.2px normal weight the text is not large, so 4.5:1 applies, and Understanding 1.4.3 says the criterion covers placeholder text. The full-page screenshot shows the compact sticky header instead of this field.
